A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CLIBD, with matching authors, core methodology and datasets. Their readable text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original BIOSCAN-1M retrieval/classification experiments, INSECT zero-shot classification results, ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and adds SimCLR and frozen-encoder comparisons, further training-strategy experiments, and computational/storage measurements.

M1.justification: The core three-encoder contrastive objective and retrieval/IS+DU inference procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B.1.1 adds an optional CLIBD training variant that performs image-only SimCLR pretraining before joint multimodal alignment, introducing a limited additional training stage.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate insect taxonomic classification and retrieval using BIOSCAN-1M and INSECT. New experiments retain this coverage. Field imagery, other biological applications and larger datasets are discussed but are not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: v4 adds a SimCLR-trained image-only baseline to Tables 1 and 8–10, and ImageBind-style alternatives that align DNA with frozen BioCLIP image/text encoders in Table 12. These substantially broaden comparisons with alternative learning strategies. Existing BioCLIP, BZSL and encoder comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New supplementary experiments introduce SimCLR augmentation/initialization controls and frozen-encoder configurations. Appendix D.4 adds computational profiling with batches of 500 and storage analysis of 84,450 records. Existing benchmark splits, top-1 metrics, main training budget and threshold-selection procedure remain unchanged; the added BZSL tuning description does not establish a protocol revision.

E4.justification: New experiments test whether gains exceed image-only domain adaptation, whether SimCLR initialization helps, and whether DNA-only alignment to frozen encoders suffices. Appendix B.4 adds retrieved-neighbor evidence to existing attention examples, while Appendix D.4 adds resource analyses. The earlier temperature, AMP, LoRA, batch-size and larger-encoder analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already report four random-seed training runs and the same Figure 9 mean curves with shaded uncertainty. v4 adds no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v4 adds SimCLR, initialization, frozen-alignment, broader BioCLIP and resource results. For retained settings, Table 2 changes trimodal image-to-text harmonic-mean accuracy from 10.2% to 8.9%. Table 4 changes fine-tuned BarcodeBERT/CLIBD-I from 23.8% to 31.2%, and CLIBD-D/RN-101 without fine-tuning from 29.3% to 26.4%. These are revised reported values; the best INSECT harmonic mean remains 35.0%.

T1.justification: The symmetric pairwise contrastive losses and their three-modality sum are mathematically unchanged; image-embedding notation changes from X to V. Neither version supplies theoretical results or proofs that are added or revised in v4.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the first-use claim from contrastive fusion of DNA and images generally to barcode DNA and images. The conclusion explicitly adds the benefit of scarce text-encoded taxonomic labels. The central multimodal-alignment and zero-shot claims, including the over-8% statement, remain.

C2.justification: Appendix D substantially expands applicability limits: laboratory-to-field transfer, barcode errors and hybridization, limited barcode coverage, and the mismatch between held-out species and truly undiscovered species. It also explains expert verification and deployment boundaries. Elsewhere, v4 interprets the SimCLR controls, emphasizes trimodal attention interpretability, and discusses BZSL tuning sensitivity.

D1.justification: v4 adds the SimCLR augmentation recipe, clarifies barcode-pretraining provenance and non-overlap, and describes BZSL validation tuning using the original search space with roughly four hours of search. Appendix D.4 supplies tokenization, parameter, runtime and storage details. Core implementation settings and the project-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v4 explicitly acknowledges earlier image/genetics and histology contrastive work, including ContIG and studies by Xie and Min, and distinguishes CLIBD through barcode-based taxonomy. It also adds positioning against SimCLR and ImageBind and substantially expands biological grounding through literature on barcode limitations, repositories and applications.

P1.justification: The main six-section organization and most existing exposition remain recognizable. v4 makes localized terminology and paragraph revisions, rewrites the conclusion, subdivides Appendix B.1, and switches to numerical citations. Appendix D adds a dedicated discussion without extensively reorganizing the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adopts the ICLR page format, redraws the partition diagram and class-size plots, replaces Figure 3 retrieval examples, and expands comparison tables. Existing attention examples are regrouped across Figures 11–13 with added nearest-retrieval images, and Figure 14 introduces a modality overview. These are substantial display and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: The added controls strengthen attribution of gains to cross-modal learning, while the narrower novelty claim and Appendix D improve scientific qualification and practical context. The established evaluation remains largely intact. Reporting is still imperfect: new Table 13 lists a genus image-to-text row with 81.9% for both seen and unseen accuracy but a 29.7% harmonic mean. Overall, the evidence supports a useful, limited improvement in rigor and clarity.
